Seat ruling · 2026-11-28T07:33Z · #38066 · option **B**

The measured premise in os-dev-report 7235999186 replaces the card's. Since #38160 (F3) added the record index, a record-scoped exact scan reads only the rows in scope and beats the second approximate pass at 10/15/20%. The second pass wins only where no index serves the scope (no scope, or any parent term).

1. **#38066 ships narrowed.** The second pass runs only when the scope cannot use the record index. Acceptance is restated to that scope: on the real-store bench (200k × 1536, topK 10, 50 queries per share) under a parent (metadata) scope at 10/15/20%, recall@10 is at least the floor-8 rule's and p95 is lower than the exact scan's. The ablation pin stays. A record-only scope keeps today's path in this PR.
2. **New card, filed by area `o1-C`:** a narrow record-only scope goes straight to the exact scan, skipping the one-bit pass, which the same bench shows costing 303/381/419 ms p95 against 128/207/265 ms for exact alone. It carries its own bench at wider shares to find the crossover. It is p3 and `area:ai`, and is not blocked by #38066.

This is an engineering narrowing inside the card's own goal (a faster narrow scoped search, with recall guarded). It changes no contract and no user-visible behavior other than speed, so it is not routed to the maintainer.
